name: Mbowe
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only ELAR deposit 'Preliminary Documentation of Mbowe' (SOAS) and classification notes; no published phonology found

sources.citation: Ohannessian, Sirarpi & Mubanga E. Kashoki (eds.). 1978. Language in Zambia. London: International African Institute. Ch. 3 'A general sketch of the Bantu languages of Zambia', sec. 3.4 'Tone and Stress' (the text).
sources.note: Generic statement for 'Zambian languages' only: syllables 'more or less evenly stressed', in some (e.g. Cewa) the penultimate has slightly greater force, coinciding with penultimate lengthening; stress never distinctive. Mbowe is mentioned only for having dental fricatives (p.68) and in Fortune's lexicostatistic table (Luyana-Mbowe 88%). Nothing Mbowe-specific on stress.

sources.citation: Jacottet, Edouard. 1896. Etudes sur les langues du Haut-Zambeze. Premiere partie: Grammaires Soubiya et Louyi. Paris: Ernest Leroux. (archive.org Google scan tudessurleslang00jacogoog, scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: RELATED VARIETY, NOT MBOWE: for Luyi (K.31, glottocode luya1241), Grammaire Louyi p.83 sec.6: 'L'accent tonique retombe toujours sur la penultieme. Ex.: munu, homme; vusiku, nuit.. Les monosyllabes sont soit enclitiques, soit proclitiques.. Quelques verbes monosyllabiques sont cependant accentues' = penultimate accent. Vowels described (p.~82, l.1611) as long when accented, short otherwise.

sources.citation: Kabimbi, Musangu Kenneth. 2014. Functions of Siluyana and Cilunda royal court languages at Lealui and Mwansabombwe palaces in Zambia: a comparative study. MA dissertation, University of Zambia.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.22 summarises Lisimba 1982 second-hand: 13 siLuyana dialects incl. Mbowe compared lexically, morphologically and phonologically; 'the only difference between these dialects and languages exist at the tonal level'. Confirms Lisimba 1982 contains Mbowe phonology/tone.
